audit.whatIsWrong: The entire content layer described a version of Aurelion Sol that does not exist. It named Starsurge, Voice of Light, Celestial Expansion and Comet of the Legend — none of which are in his kit — across spikes[0..3], early, mid, late, wants.you and wants.foe.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon gives Cosmic Creator (P, permanent Stardust stacks), Breath of Light (Q, 3s, 750, channel), Astral Flight (W, 22/20.5/19/17.5/16, 1500, flies over terrain), Singularity (E, 12s, 750, black hole that pulls and executes below a health threshold), and Falling Star / The Skies Descend (R, 120/110/100, 1250, stun).
audit.corrected: Every fabricated name replaced with the real ability and the real number. The packet defect 'never names any of Aurelion Sol's abilities' is now answered.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three decisive interactions were absent: Petrifying Gaze cancels his channels; Singularity is percent-health and executes; Astral Flight crosses terrain to cut a dashless champion's retreat.
audit.why: Breath of Light and Astral Flight both carry the channel flag ('interruptible — any CC cancels it') and your R is hard CC. Singularity carries percentHealth + execute. Astral Flight carries terrain and 1500 range. All three are flagged in _missing for this pair.
audit.corrected: Gaze-cancels-channel written into phases[4].why, dosFull[1].d, spikes[1], mid and wants.you[2]; the execute into dontsFull[1].d, spikes[2] and report[8]; the terrain retreat-cut into phases[6].why and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer said Cassiopeia wins all seven rows while the full layer said Skill on 3, 4 and 5 and Aurelion Sol on 6 — four rows rendering two answers.
audit.why: The full layer is right and is grounded: Singularity's 12s pull-and-execute evens levels 4-5, level 6 is a mirror (his stun vs your channel-cancel), and Cosmic Creator's Stardust is permanent so his scaling beats a one-off item spike.
audit.corrected: win[3], win[4], win[5] -> Skill and win[6] -> Aurelion Sol, each with a rewritten whys and a rewritten full-layer why.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit and dosFull[2].d invented a 'fifteen-second' Astral Flight.
audit.why: Astral Flight is 22s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5. Breath of Light 3s, Singularity 12s, Falling Star 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and ahead.

edits.before: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots (Tear first back). Seraph's into Liandry's, then Rabadon's; Zhonya's vs dive. No boots — her passive replaces them; spend the slot on damage.
edits.after: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots (Tear first back). Seraph's into Liandry's, then Rabadon's; Zhonya's answers Falling Star. Singularity is percent-health, so MR alone will not save you.

edits.before: Aurelion Sol needs to charge Starsurge for several seconds before it threatens real damage, giving you free windows to poke with Noxious Blast whenever his stars aren't fully wound up.
edits.after: Aurelion Sol has to hold Breath of Light on you for seconds to get paid, and it only reaches 750 — step out of the beam and poke from 850 while his Stardust stalls out.

edits.before: His Voice of Light knockup enables a combo, but the cast time is long and Twin Fang stacks already applied before he lands it mean you win most trades if he tries to all-in.
edits.after: Falling Star, not 'Voice of Light', is his 6: a 1250-range stun on 120s. Your Gaze cancels channels, so hold it for the moment he commits Astral Flight rather than spending it on poke.

edits.before: Once you have your core item, your DPS uptime through his Celestial Expansion zone outpaces his ramping poke, and Miasma denies him easy Starsurge setups.
edits.after: Once you have your core item, poison uptime beats his ramp — but Singularity's centre executes under a health threshold, so never fang him from inside the black hole.

edits.before: Cassiopeia's sustained damage and mobility via Twin Fang range consistently outclass his clunky, cast-time-heavy poke kit in extended lane and skirmish situations.
edits.after: Cosmic Creator's Stardust is permanent, so his numbers only grow — late you need the fight to start on your terms, with the Gaze already cancelling one of his channels.

edits.before: Cassiopeia wins this lane clearly from level 1 — Aurelion Sol's kit is entirely built around slow setup and long cast times, meaning your immediate Noxious Blast poke punishes him every time he tries to charge a star or wind up Starsurge. He has almost no early trading power against your instant-cast poke.
edits.after: Cassiopeia wins early — Breath of Light is a channel he has to hold on you from 750 while your Noxious Blast reaches 850, so every attempt to bank Stardust costs him health. Punish each channel, shove the wave he needs to stack Cosmic Creator, and he has almost no early trading power against your instant poke.

edits.before: This lead only grows through levels 4-6 as your combo damage scales while his kit remains reliant on landing a difficult stun to do anything meaningful, and his level 6 combo is easily played around once you've pre-applied Twin Fang stacks. He's forced into a purely passive, farm-only lane phase.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 tighten instead. Singularity arrives on a 12s cooldown: it drags you toward its centre and executes below a health threshold, so it is not a zone you fang from. Your answer is Petrifying Gaze, which cancels both of his channels — hold it for his Astral Flight commit, not for the wave.

edits.before: With items, Cassiopeia's sustained DPS and zone denial via Miasma completely outclass his ramping, cast-time-dependent poke — he simply can't out-damage your uptime in any prolonged exchange. He's reduced to hoping for a lucky long-range Starsurge pick rather than contesting lane directly.
edits.after: Late, Cosmic Creator's Stardust has been stacking all game and never resets, while Astral Flight crosses terrain at 1500 range to open fights you have no dash to walk away from. You still out-tick him in a straight exchange, but he chooses when the exchange starts — keep vision and save the Gaze for his channel.

notes: This matchup's content layer was written against a pre-rework Aurelion Sol — Starsurge, Voice of Light, Celestial Expansion and Comet of the Legend are all fabricated relative to the current kit. Every one is replaced. UNVERIFIED and deliberately not asserted: whether Miasma's grounding prevents Astral Flight. Astral Flight carries terrain + channel flags but no dash flag, and Riot's text does not say it is a movement ability, so phases[1].why was rewritten to avoid the claim; dosFull[2].t ('Ground his retreat path with W') is generic and was left as-is rather than guessed at. Rows 0-2 already agreed across layers.
